title: 100 Ready-to-Use Replies
subtitle: Calm, clear wording for the moments when you need the right sentence fast. A companion to Shadow Persuasion: The Hidden Rules of Power.

intro.heading: How to use this
intro.html: This is a phrasebook for hard moments. Each of the 100 replies covers one real situation, at work, with a partner, an ex, family, friends, money or a group, and gives you three ways to say it. Find your situation in one of the two indexes below, pick the wording that sounds most like you, and change any words that don’t fit. Most replies are short, because a short, calm sentence gives the other person less to argue with. But no wording works every time, and none of these is a magic line. They are a starting point, so that when your mind goes blank you still have something steady to say.

intro.heading: How each reply is set up
intro.html:
• The situation in one line, as the heading.
  • The task: what the reply is for. Asking, declining, clarifying, trading, following up or repairing.
  • Three wording options for the same situation, built on the same facts and the same request. Usually warm, direct and final. “Final” never means a threat. It means closing the exchange or saying what you will do next. Requests, apologies and confirmations don’t need a harder version, so those get other options, such as a written or text version. When an option belongs to a later moment (after the meeting, later in private, after a second ask, or once you’ve both agreed), its label says so.
  • When it fits: when to use it, and when not to.

intro.heading: A few things that help
intro.html:
Use a “Confirming” option only after both people have agreed to those terms. If a date, task or condition is new, present it as a proposal.

  1. Say it once, then pause. Extra reasons and apologies give people more to push against. A short silence after a calm sentence is fine.
  2. If they push, you can repeat yourself. You don’t need a new argument each time. Often the same sentence, in the same tone, is enough. If it isn’t, that’s the moment for The No-Agreement Plan: what you will do if the answer is still no (Chapter 28, When They Still Say No).
  3. Make it yours. If a line sounds stiff in your mouth, change the words and keep the shape.
  4. Check that it’s fair. Every reply here passes The Four Fair Influence Tests: Is it honest? Do they know what they are agreeing to? Can they make a real choice without unfair pressure or punishment? Am I using my power responsibly? Keep it that way when you adapt them.
  5. Records stay private. Several replies suggest confirming things in writing or saving messages. Keep anything you save somewhere only you can reach, not on a shared phone, shared computer or shared account. Remember that work email and work devices can usually be read by your employer.

intro.heading: When words are not the answer
intro.html:
There are no scripts in this guide for threats, violence or fear, on purpose. If someone is threatening you, hurting you, following or tracking you, checking your phone, or controlling your money, a better sentence is not what will help. Confronting them, even with someone else in the room, is not a safety plan.

Instead:

  • Read Chapter 11, When Pressure Becomes Danger.
  • In the US, contact the National Domestic Violence Hotline: call 1-800-799-7233, or text START to 88788. You don’t have to be sure it “counts.” Men contact them too.
  • If you are in immediate danger, call 911.
  • If someone may be checking your phone, contact help from a device they can’t reach, such as a friend’s phone, a work phone or a library computer.
  • If someone threatens you or your job at work, keep notes somewhere safe (not on work devices), and talk to HR or an employment lawyer.
  • If you, or someone you are talking with, have thoughts of suicide or self-harm, that is a different kind of help. Call or text the 988 Suicide and Crisis Lifeline (988 in the US). If someone threatens to hurt themselves to make you do something, take the threat seriously, contact 988 or 911, and see Chapter 11.

Outside the US, local hotlines and support services exist in most countries.

groups.name: An ex (practical matters)
groups.note: These replies are for everyday, practical contact: belongings, handovers, schedules and arrangements you’ve already agreed. Anything involving custody, support or a formal agreement is a legal matter. Talk to a family lawyer. Keep messages with an ex short and factual, and save them somewhere your ex can’t reach, not on a shared phone, tablet or account.

replies.title: Your manager adds a new project when you are already full

options.label: Warm
options.text: I'd like to do this well. To fit it in, which of my current projects should move back?

options.label: Direct
options.text: I'm at capacity. If this comes first, the monthly report slips to next Friday. Is that the trade you want?

options.label: Final
options.text: I can't add it without dropping something. Tell me which one moves, and I'll let the people waiting on it know.

replies.whenItFits: You really are full, and your manager sets priorities. Bring your current list so the choice is concrete (Chapter 23, Work, Pay, and Recognition).
replies.whenItFitsText: You really are full, and your manager sets priorities. Bring your current list so the choice is concrete (Chapter 23, Work, Pay, and Recognition).

replies.title: A coworker repeats your idea in a meeting and gets the credit

options.label: Warm
options.text: Glad that's getting traction. It builds on what I raised earlier, so let me add the next step I had in mind.

options.label: Direct
options.text: That's the point I made a few minutes ago. I'd like to walk everyone through how I'd run it.

options.label: Final (to your manager, after the meeting)
options.text: The scheduling idea I raised today ended up credited to someone else. I'd like to lead it. Can we talk this week?

replies.whenItFits: Say it calmly in the moment and add something new, so you are linked to the work. The aim is credit, not shaming anyone. If it keeps happening, use the third line.
replies.whenItFitsText: Say it calmly in the moment and add something new, so you are linked to the work. The aim is credit, not shaming anyone. If it keeps happening, use the third line.

replies.title: Your manager sends your work upward without your name on it
replies.short: Your work sent up without your name

options.label: Warm
options.text: I was glad to see the analysis go to leadership. Next time, could I present the part I built?

options.label: Direct
options.text: The analysis went up without my name. I'd like to be credited on work I lead. Can we agree on that from now on?

options.label: Final
options.text: For the next phase, I'll put my name and the date on each draft I share, so it's clear who built what.

replies.whenItFits: Ask for a specific change going forward rather than an apology for the past. Keep your own dated copies of your work, but remember that work email and work devices can usually be read by your employer.
replies.whenItFitsText: Ask for a specific change going forward rather than an apology for the past. Keep your own dated copies of your work, but remember that work email and work devices can usually be read by your employer.

replies.title: A coworker writes up shared work as if it were theirs alone
replies.short: Shared work written up as theirs

options.label: Warm (privately)
options.text: In the update, the project read as yours alone. Next time, can we list who did which part?

options.label: Direct (to the team)
options.text: Quick note so the record is complete: I did the vendor research and the budget on this one.

options.label: Final
options.text: From now on I'll send a short update on my own parts, so neither of us has to speak for the other.

replies.whenItFits: Start privately if it might have been careless rather than deliberate. Go to the team version only if the private word didn’t change anything.
replies.whenItFitsText: Start privately if it might have been careless rather than deliberate. Go to the team version only if the private word didn't change anything.

replies.title: Asking for a meeting about a raise

options.label: Warm
options.text: I'd like thirty minutes in the next two weeks to talk about my pay and my role.

options.label: Direct
options.text: I'd like to discuss a raise. I'll bring what I've taken on this year and what similar roles pay.

options.label: By email
options.text: Could we book a time before budgets are set to talk about my compensation? Any slot next week works for me.

replies.whenItFits: Ask for the meeting first, then make your case in the meeting. Find out who actually approves raises, so you are talking to someone who can say yes.
replies.whenItFitsText: Ask for the meeting first, then make your case in the meeting. Find out who actually approves raises, so you are talking to someone who can say yes.

replies.title: The answer on your raise is "not right now"

options.label: Warm
options.text: Thanks for being straight with me. What would need to be true for this to happen at my next review?

options.label: Direct
options.text: Can we agree on the specific goals and a date to revisit this, and put both in an email?

options.label: Final (once you've agreed goals and a date)
options.text: I understand. I'll send a note with what we agreed, and I'll bring it up again on that date.

replies.whenItFits: A “not now” with no date often turns into a quiet no. Have The No-Agreement Plan (what you will do if the answer is still no) ready before the meeting (Chapter 28, When They Still Say No).
replies.whenItFitsText: A "not now" with no date often turns into a quiet no. Have The No-Agreement Plan (what you will do if the answer is still no) ready before the meeting (Chapter 28, When They Still Say No).

replies.title: Your role has grown, but your title and pay haven't

options.label: Warm
options.text: Over the past year I've picked up scheduling and training. I'd like my title and pay to reflect that.

options.label: Direct
options.text: I'm doing two roles' worth of work. Either we adjust my pay and title, or some of these duties move to someone else.

options.label: Final (if the raise is turned down)
options.text: If a raise isn't possible this year, I'd like to hand training back by March. Can we plan how?

replies.whenItFits: Offering two fair options is not a threat, as long as you would genuinely accept either one. Don’t name an option you aren’t ready to follow through on.
replies.whenItFitsText: Offering two fair options is not a threat, as long as you would genuinely accept either one. Don't name an option you aren't ready to follow through on.

replies.title: A request to work this weekend

options.label: Warm
options.text: I'm not available this weekend. I can pick it up first thing Monday.

options.label: Direct
options.text: I keep my weekends clear. If it's truly urgent, let's look at what can wait so this fits in on Monday.

options.label: Final
options.text: I won't be working this weekend. I'll pick it up Monday morning.

replies.whenItFits: Ordinary requests. In a real emergency, or if weekends are part of your role, a trade (time off later) may fit better.
replies.whenItFitsText: Ordinary requests. In a real emergency, or if weekends are part of your role, a trade (time off later) may fit better.

replies.title: A coworker asks you to cover their shift again

options.label: Warm
options.text: I've covered a few times lately, so I need to pass on this one. I hope you find someone.

options.label: Direct
options.text: I can't cover again. Have you checked with the shift lead?

options.label: Final
options.text: I won't be covering this shift. Please ask someone else.

replies.whenItFits: A pattern of asks, not a real emergency. Don’t make up a conflict. A made-up reason can be checked, and it invites “Then how about next week?”
replies.whenItFitsText: A pattern of asks, not a real emergency. Don't make up a conflict. A made-up reason can be checked, and it invites "Then how about next week?"

replies.title: A big task lands on your desk at 4:40 on a Friday

options.label: Warm
options.text: I can start it Monday morning and have it to you by noon. Does that work?

options.label: Direct
options.text: I can't do it properly before I leave today. If something is truly urgent, what's the smallest piece you need tonight?

options.label: Final
options.text: I'm leaving at five. It'll be the first thing I open on Monday.

replies.whenItFits: When the deadline is a habit, not a crisis. Asking for “the smallest piece” often shows how much of the urgency is real.
replies.whenItFitsText: When the deadline is a habit, not a crisis. Asking for "the smallest piece" often shows how much of the urgency is real.

replies.title: A hint that your review could suffer if you say no

options.label: Warm
options.text: I want to make sure I understand. Is my review tied to taking this on?

options.label: Direct
options.text: Can you tell me exactly how this affects my review? I'd like to know where I stand.

options.label: Final
options.text: I'll send a short email afterward so we both have the same understanding.

replies.whenItFits: Use these questions only if you feel safe asking and the comment is unclear. If it becomes a threat or you fear retaliation, skip further scripts and see Chapter 11, When Pressure Becomes Danger. Keep any notes private and seek HR, union or employment advice suited to the situation.

replies.title: You are criticized in front of the team
replies.short: Criticized in front of the team

options.label: Warm
options.text: I'd like to understand that properly. Can we talk one-on-one after this?

options.label: Direct
options.text: I'm happy to go through the problem. I'd rather do it privately.

options.label: Later, in private
options.text: About this morning: I want to fix the issue you raised. I'd also ask that feedback like that come to me privately first.

replies.whenItFits: Don’t argue the details in front of everyone. If the criticism was fair, say so when you meet.
replies.whenItFitsText: Don't argue the details in front of everyone. If the criticism was fair, say so when you meet.

replies.title: Confirming what was agreed after a meeting

options.label: Warm
options.text: Thanks for today. To make sure I got it right: I'll draft the plan by the 12th, and you'll get budget sign-off by the 15th.

options.label: Direct
options.text: Confirming what we agreed: the draft is mine, due the 12th. Sign-off is yours, due the 15th. Let me know by Friday if anything is off.

options.label: Short message
options.text: Just so we're aligned: I'm doing the draft, you're getting sign-off. Right?

replies.whenItFits: After any agreement. This is The Smallest Agreed Step (a useful next action, with clear agreement on exactly what it covers) in writing (Chapter 22, Turn Agreement Into Action). Keep your copy private, and remember your employer may read work email.

replies.title: You've stopped being invited to meetings you used to attend

options.label: Warm
options.text: I noticed I'm not on the planning invites anymore. Was that on purpose? I'd like to stay involved.

options.label: Direct
options.text: I need to be in the planning meetings to do my part well. Can you add me back?

options.label: Final (after a vague answer)
options.text: If there's a reason I'm being left out, I'd rather hear it directly so I can fix it.

replies.whenItFits: Start warm; invite lists change for dull reasons. Use the final line only after vague answers.
replies.whenItFitsText: Start warm; invite lists change for dull reasons. Use the final line only after vague answers.

replies.title: Your manager's expectations are vague

options.label: Warm
options.text: When you say 'more ownership', what would that look like day to day?

options.label: Direct
options.text: What would a great result on this project look like by the end of the quarter?

options.label: By email
options.text: To make sure I'm working on the right things, could you list your top three priorities for me this month?

replies.whenItFits: Before you are judged on something nobody defined. Open questions get you real information, not a yes or no (Chapter 14, Ask Questions That Open the Problem).
replies.whenItFitsText: Before you are judged on something nobody defined. Open questions get you real information, not a yes or no (Chapter 14, Ask Questions That Open the Problem).

replies.title: Taking back a yes you gave too fast at work
replies.short: Withdrawing a rushed yes at work

options.label: Warm
options.text: I said yes to the event committee too quickly. Looking at my workload, I can't do it well. I'm sorry for the back-and-forth.

options.label: Direct
options.text: I need to take back my yes on the committee. I can help find someone else this week.

options.label: Final
options.text: I'm stepping off the committee. I'll hand over my notes by Friday.

replies.whenItFits: When you need to step out of the commitment completely. Do it as early as possible, before others plan around you. Offering a handover makes it fair. Groveling doesn’t. To keep part of a yes instead, see Reply 76.

replies.title: Asking a busy colleague for help
replies.short: Asking a busy colleague for help

options.label: Warm
options.text: Could you spare fifteen minutes this week to look over my numbers? You're better at this than I am.

options.label: Direct
options.text: I need help with the model before Thursday. Is there a time that works, or someone else you'd suggest?

options.label: Short message
options.text: No pressure if this week is bad, but could you look at one spreadsheet for me?

replies.whenItFits: This is The Clean Ask: say what you want, give the relevant reason, leave room for a real answer. Mean the “no pressure” (Chapter 20, Build Allies Without Creating Debts).
replies.whenItFitsText: This is The Clean Ask: say what you want, give the relevant reason, leave room for a real answer. Mean the "no pressure" (Chapter 20, Build Allies Without Creating Debts).

replies.title: You snapped at a coworker
replies.short: After you snapped at a coworker

options.label: Warm
options.text: I was short with you this morning when you asked about the file. That wasn't fair to you. I'm sorry.

options.label: Direct
options.text: I'm sorry I snapped earlier. Can we start again? What do you need from me on the file?

options.label: Short message
options.text: Sorry about earlier. That was on me. Happy to go through the file whenever suits you.

replies.whenItFits: Soon, ideally the same day. At work, a short apology and a fresh start on the task usually do more than a long talk. Skip “but you” in the apology. That turns it into round two.
replies.whenItFitsText: Soon, ideally the same day. At work, a short apology and a fresh start on the task usually do more than a long talk. Skip "but you" in the apology. That turns it into round two.

replies.title: Someone who reports to you keeps missing deadlines

options.label: Warm
options.text: The last two reports came in late. What's getting in the way?

options.label: Direct
options.text: I need these by noon on Fridays. What would help you hit that?

options.label: Final
options.text: If Friday noon won't work, tell me now and we'll change the plan. If it will, I'm going to count on it.

replies.whenItFits: When you hold the authority. Ask before you assume; the cause may be your process (Chapter 21, Lead Without Making People Dependent).
replies.whenItFitsText: When you hold the authority. Ask before you assume; the cause may be your process (Chapter 21, Lead Without Making People Dependent).

replies.title: A coworker keeps passing small tasks to you ("You're so good at this")

options.label: Warm
options.text: Thanks, that's kind. Let me show you how to do it once, so you can handle it next time.

options.label: Direct
options.text: I can't take this on. The step-by-step guide is in the shared folder.

options.label: Final (if they keep coming)
options.text: I'm going to stop doing these for the team. I'll let our manager know so they get assigned properly.

replies.whenItFits: Compliments are nice. They are not a job description. Teaching once is generous; doing it forever is a role you never agreed to.
replies.whenItFitsText: Compliments are nice. They are not a job description. Teaching once is generous; doing it forever is a role you never agreed to.

replies.title: Asking your partner to take over a chore you always end up doing
replies.short: Sharing a chore you always do

options.label: Warm
options.text: I've been doing the bills and the school forms for a long time. Could you take over the bills?

options.label: Direct
options.text: I'd like us to split the household paperwork. Can you take the bills starting next month?

options.label: Follow-up
options.text: Last week we said you'd take the bills. Have you had a chance to set up the payments?

replies.whenItFits: Ask for one named task, not “more help”. A specific ask is easier to say yes to and easier to check on later.
replies.whenItFitsText: Ask for one named task, not "more help". A specific ask is easier to say yes to and easier to check on later.

replies.title: Your partner goes quiet after a disagreement

options.label: Warm
options.text: I can tell you're upset. When you're ready, could we talk tonight after dinner?

options.label: Direct
options.text: I'd like us to talk about yesterday, even if it's hard. Can we do it tonight after dinner?

options.label: Final (if the silence goes on)
options.text: I'm not going to keep guessing. When you want to talk, tell me and I'll make the time.

replies.whenItFits: Space to cool down is fine. Silence used as pressure is different (Chapter 9, Silence, Distance, and Conditional Warmth). Don’t chase.
replies.whenItFitsText: Space to cool down is fine. Silence used as pressure is different (Chapter 9, Silence, Distance, and Conditional Warmth). Don't chase.

replies.title: Warmth is withheld until you apologize

options.label: Warm
options.text: I miss feeling close to you. I want to fix this, but not by apologizing for something I don't think I did.

options.label: Direct
options.text: I don't want closeness between us to depend on me always agreeing.

options.label: Final
options.text: I'm sorry we're both hurting. I'm still not going to apologize just to end the silence.

replies.whenItFits: When you honestly don’t think you were wrong. If you were partly wrong, apologize for that part (Reply 32). If coldness comes with threats or control, see Chapter 11.
replies.whenItFitsText: When you honestly don't think you were wrong. If you were partly wrong, apologize for that part (Reply 32). If coldness comes with threats or control, see Chapter 11.

replies.title: "You're too sensitive"

options.label: Warm
options.text: Maybe I am. It still hurt, and I want you to know that.

options.label: Direct
options.text: Sensitive or not, I'm asking you not to say that to me again.

options.label: Final
options.text: I've told you how it lands. I'm not going to argue about whether I'm allowed to feel it.

replies.whenItFits: You don’t have to win a debate about your personality. The request (“don’t say that again”) is what matters.
replies.whenItFitsText: You don't have to win a debate about your personality. The request ("don't say that again") is what matters.

replies.title: "That never happened"

options.label: Warm
options.text: We remember it differently. Can we talk about what we each want next time instead?

options.label: Direct
options.text: I'm not going to argue about last week. Going forward, I need plans to be talked about before they're made.

options.label: Final
options.text: I know what I heard. I won't debate it, and I won't pretend it didn't happen either.

replies.whenItFits: You don’t have to win the argument about the past (Chapter 8, When the Story Keeps Changing). If it happens often, keep short dated notes where only you can see them, not on a shared device.
replies.whenItFitsText: You don't have to win the argument about the past (Chapter 8, When the Story Keeps Changing). If it happens often, keep short dated notes where only you can see them, not on a shared device.

replies.title: "It was just a joke"

options.label: Warm
options.text: That one hurt. Please leave it out.

options.label: Direct
options.text: It didn't land as a joke for me. Please don't say it again.

options.label: Final (if it happens again)
options.text: If it comes up again in front of people, I'm going to say so right then.

replies.whenItFits: One clumsy joke deserves the warm line. The same joke after you’ve asked twice deserves the final one, said calmly.
replies.whenItFitsText: One clumsy joke deserves the warm line. The same joke after you've asked twice deserves the final one, said calmly.

replies.title: Your partner makes a big money decision without you

options.label: Warm
options.text: I'd like to be part of decisions like this. Can we agree to talk first for anything over $500?

options.label: Direct
options.text: I wasn't asked about the new car. From now on, let's agree that anything over $500 is decided together.

options.label: Final
options.text: Until we've agreed how we decide these things, I'm not signing off on anything new.

replies.whenItFits: The $500 is only an example. If money is hidden from you, or you’re kept from your own accounts, see Chapter 11 instead.
replies.whenItFitsText: The $500 is only an example. If money is hidden from you, or you're kept from your own accounts, see Chapter 11 instead.

replies.title: Proposing a fair trade on time

options.label: Warm
options.text: Go to the lake on Saturday. Could I have Thursday evenings for my class?

options.label: Direct
options.text: I'll cover the kids on Saturday so you can go to the lake. In return, I'd like Thursday evenings for my class.

options.label: Confirming
options.text: So: lake Saturday for you, Thursdays for me, starting this week. Right?

replies.whenItFits: Trades work best when both sides get something they actually want. Confirm it out loud, or it fades by the next week.
replies.whenItFitsText: Trades work best when both sides get something they actually want. Confirm it out loud, or it fades by the next week.

replies.title: The same old fight is starting again

options.label: Warm
options.text: We're starting the same fight. Can we stop here and come back to it on Saturday?

options.label: Direct
options.text: We keep having this one. Let's take a calm hour on Saturday and actually solve it.

options.label: Final
options.text: I'm going to stop for tonight. I'll bring it up again Saturday morning.

replies.whenItFits: Use it early, before voices rise. The final line only works if you really do bring it up on Saturday. Otherwise it becomes a dodge.
replies.whenItFitsText: Use it early, before voices rise. The final line only works if you really do bring it up on Saturday. Otherwise it becomes a dodge.

replies.title: Your partner raises their voice

options.label: Warm
options.text: I want to hear you. I can't while we're shouting.

options.label: Direct
options.text: Please lower your voice, or let's stop for now.

options.label: Final (if it keeps going)
options.text: I'm going to step out for a while. We can pick this up tomorrow.

replies.whenItFits: An ordinary heated argument. If there is fear, threats, breaking things or blocking you from leaving, skip the script and see “When words are not the answer” and Chapter 11.
replies.whenItFitsText: An ordinary heated argument. If there is fear, threats, breaking things or blocking you from leaving, skip the script and see "When words are not the answer" and Chapter 11.

replies.title: A new partner is moving very fast

options.label: Warm
options.text: I really like spending time with you. I'd like to take things a bit slower.

options.label: Direct
options.text: Moving in after two months is too fast for me. Let's see where we are by the summer.

options.label: Final
options.text: I've told you the pace I'm comfortable with. If that doesn't work for you, I understand.

replies.whenItFits: Fast isn’t always a warning sign. How they take the slower pace tells you more than the words (Chapter 25, Dating, Intimacy, and Difficult Relationships).
replies.whenItFitsText: Fast isn't always a warning sign. How they take the slower pace tells you more than the words (Chapter 25, Dating, Intimacy, and Difficult Relationships).

replies.title: Repairing after you were harsh with your partner

options.label: Warm
options.text: I said something cruel last night, and I'm sorry. You didn't deserve that.

options.label: Direct
options.text: What I said about your job was cruel, and it isn't what I think. I'm sorry.

options.label: Short message
options.text: I was out of line last night. I'm sorry. When you're ready, I'd like to hear how it landed.

replies.whenItFits: Name the exact thing you said, without explaining it away. Then let them take the time they need; an apology doesn’t come with a deadline for forgiveness. A repair is about what you said, not a new round of who started it.
replies.whenItFitsText: Name the exact thing you said, without explaining it away. Then let them take the time they need; an apology doesn't come with a deadline for forgiveness. A repair is about what you said, not a new round of who started it.

replies.title: Asking for regular time together

options.label: Warm
options.text: I miss you. Could we keep Friday nights for just the two of us?

options.label: Direct
options.text: We've been passing like roommates. I'd like Friday nights to be ours, phones away.

options.label: Confirming
options.text: So Fridays are ours. I'll book the sitter for this week.

replies.whenItFits: Ask for what you want, not a list of what’s missing. “I miss you” opens a door. “You never make time for me” closes one.
replies.whenItFitsText: Ask for what you want, not a list of what's missing. "I miss you" opens a door. "You never make time for me" closes one.

replies.title: Your ex wants to reopen something already agreed

options.label: Warm
options.text: I know you'd like a different split. We agreed on this in June, and I want to keep to it.

options.label: Direct
options.text: That's settled. I'm not reopening it.

options.label: Final
options.text: My answer on this hasn't changed. I'm ending this conversation for today.

replies.whenItFits: Informal arrangements you both agreed to. If it’s a court order or a legal agreement, don’t negotiate it by text; talk to a family lawyer.
replies.whenItFitsText: Informal arrangements you both agreed to. If it's a court order or a legal agreement, don't negotiate it by text; talk to a family lawyer.

replies.title: Your ex asks to change the pickup time at the last minute

options.label: Warm
options.text: Sorry, I can't do 7 tonight. Next time, a day's notice gives me a chance to make a change work.

options.label: Direct
options.text: I can't change tonight. The usual time stands.

options.label: Text
options.text: Can't do 7 tonight. See you at 5:30 as planned.

replies.whenItFits: Everyday logistics. Being flexible now and then is generous; being flexible every week becomes the new schedule. Changes to a custody order are a question for a family lawyer.
replies.whenItFitsText: Everyday logistics. Being flexible now and then is generous; being flexible every week becomes the new schedule. Changes to a custody order are a question for a family lawyer.

replies.title: Your ex brings up old arguments during a practical conversation

options.label: Warm
options.text: I hear that you're still upset. Right now I'm only able to talk about Saturday.

options.label: Direct
options.text: I'm not discussing the past. Back to Saturday: are you picking up at 10?

options.label: Text
options.text: Happy to sort out the schedule. Not discussing anything else.

replies.whenItFits: Redirect once. If it keeps going, end the call and finish the logistics later by message.
replies.whenItFitsText: Redirect once. If it keeps going, end the call and finish the logistics later by message.

replies.title: Your ex still hasn't returned your belongings

options.label: Warm
options.text: Could I pick up the tools and the desk from the garage on Saturday the 20th? Morning or afternoon works.

options.label: Direct
options.text: I still need the tools and the desk. Please have them ready on Saturday the 20th. I'll bring someone to help carry.

options.label: In writing
options.text: Following up on the tools and the desk. Can you confirm that Saturday the 20th works for me to collect them?

replies.whenItFits: Name the items and a date. If you feel unsafe collecting them, skip the script and read Chapter 11, When Pressure Becomes Danger; the National Domestic Violence Hotline (1-800-799-7233, text START to 88788) can talk through safer options, from a device your ex can’t access. In immediate danger, call 911. For disputes over ownership, talk to a lawyer.
replies.whenItFitsText: Name the items and a date. If you feel unsafe collecting them, skip the script and read Chapter 11, When Pressure Becomes Danger; the National Domestic Violence Hotline (1-800-799-7233, text START to 88788) can talk through safer options, from a device your ex can't access. In immediate danger, call 911. For disputes over ownership, talk to a lawyer.

replies.title: "You agreed to this, don't you remember?" (and you didn't)

options.label: Warm
options.text: I don't remember agreeing to that. Can you show me the message where we discussed it?

options.label: Direct
options.text: That's not what I agreed to. What I agreed to was alternate holidays, starting with Thanksgiving.

options.label: Final
options.text: Let's check the original agreement. I haven't agreed to the change you're asking for.

replies.whenItFits: This is why short written confirmations help (Reply 41). Store them where your ex can’t access them.
replies.whenItFitsText: This is why short written confirmations help (Reply 41). Store them where your ex can't access them.

replies.title: Your ex asks for money outside your arrangement

options.label: Warm
options.text: I know things are tight. I'm keeping to what we agreed.

options.label: Direct
options.text: I'm not able to pay for that. It's outside our arrangement.

options.label: Final
options.text: If you want to change the arrangement, that needs to go through the proper process.

replies.whenItFits: Small, informal asks. Anything about child support or formal payments is a legal question for a family lawyer, not a text conversation.
replies.whenItFitsText: Small, informal asks. Anything about child support or formal payments is a legal question for a family lawyer, not a text conversation.

replies.title: Your ex sends a long, angry message

options.label: Warm
options.text: I read your message. To answer the practical question: Tuesday works for the vet.

options.label: Direct
options.text: I'm not going to discuss this over text. If there's a practical question, send it and I'll answer.

options.label: Final
options.text: Noted. I'll reply to logistics only.

replies.whenItFits: Answer the practical point and leave the rest. If the messages include threats, save them safely and see Chapter 11.
replies.whenItFitsText: Answer the practical point and leave the rest. If the messages include threats, save them safely and see Chapter 11.

replies.title: Proposing a simple written routine for handovers

options.label: Warm
options.text: We keep getting tangled up on handovers. Could we write down the usual times and how we change them?

options.label: Direct
options.text: I'd like us to agree that changes go by text at least a day ahead, so neither of us is caught off guard.

options.label: Confirming
options.text: Confirming what we agreed: Fridays at 5, Sundays at 6, changes by text a day ahead.

replies.whenItFits: Repeated small disputes. A written routine gives you both a clear reference. Keep your copy somewhere your ex can’t reach. If you need it to be formal or enforceable, talk to a family lawyer.
replies.whenItFitsText: Repeated small disputes. A written routine gives you both a clear reference. Keep your copy somewhere your ex can't reach. If you need it to be formal or enforceable, talk to a family lawyer.

replies.title: Your ex asks for a favor when it suits them

options.label: Warm
options.text: I can't lend the car this weekend. I hope you find another way.

options.label: Direct
options.text: I'm not lending the car. I'm keeping things simpler between us.

options.label: Final
options.text: I'll help with things that affect the kids. Other favors, I'm going to pass on.

replies.whenItFits: When favors keep flowing one way, or when a favor tends to reopen old arguments. Kind is fine. Endlessly available is a role.
replies.whenItFitsText: When favors keep flowing one way, or when a favor tends to reopen old arguments. Kind is fine. Endlessly available is a role.

replies.title: Your ex tells friends or family a different story about you
replies.short: A different story told about you

options.label: Warm (to a friend)
options.text: I know you've heard their side. I'm not going to argue it. I'd just ask you not to pass messages between us.

options.label: Direct
options.text: I'd rather not talk about the breakup. Can we talk about something else?

options.label: Final
options.text: I'm keeping the details private. That's not going to change.

replies.whenItFits: Chasing every version rarely works; steady behavior says more. If it turns into harassment, see Chapter 11.
replies.whenItFitsText: Chasing every version rarely works; steady behavior says more. If it turns into harassment, see Chapter 11.

replies.title: Your ex starts talking about "us" during practical contact

options.label: Warm
options.text: I'm glad we can be civil. I'm not open to talking about getting back together.

options.label: Direct
options.text: I'll talk about the house sale. Not about us.

options.label: Final
options.text: My answer on that is settled. Let's keep to the house sale.

replies.whenItFits: When you’re sure. If you’re unsure whether you want to reconnect, don’t answer in the middle of a logistics call. Take time to think on your own first.
replies.whenItFitsText: When you're sure. If you're unsure whether you want to reconnect, don't answer in the middle of a logistics call. Take time to think on your own first.

replies.title: A parent criticizes your choices again

options.label: Warm
options.text: I know you'd have chosen differently. I'm happy with this.

options.label: Direct
options.text: I've made my decision, and I'm not going to debate it.

options.label: Final
options.text: If this comes up again today, I'll head home and we'll catch up next week.

replies.whenItFits: The final line states your own next step, said calmly and followed through, not as punishment (Chapter 26, Family, Friends, and the Roles That Stick).
replies.whenItFitsText: The final line states your own next step, said calmly and followed through, not as punishment (Chapter 26, Family, Friends, and the Roles That Stick).

replies.title: A parent compares you with a sibling

options.label: Warm
options.text: I'm glad things are going well for him. I'd like us to talk about me without the comparison.

options.label: Direct
options.text: Please stop comparing us. It doesn't help either of us.

options.label: Final
options.text: I'm going to change the subject now. How's the garden?

replies.whenItFits: Don’t defend your record point by point. That accepts the contest. Step out of it instead.
replies.whenItFitsText: Don't defend your record point by point. That accepts the contest. Step out of it instead.

replies.title: "You never call" or "You never visit"

options.label: Warm
options.text: I can't come every week, but I'd love to call on Sundays and visit once a month. Would that work for you?

options.label: Direct
options.text: Here's what I can do: a call every Sunday and a visit on the first Saturday of the month.

options.label: Final
options.text: That's what I can manage right now. I'll call you Sunday.

replies.whenItFits: Offer something specific you will reliably do, rather than vague promises followed by guilt.
replies.whenItFitsText: Offer something specific you will reliably do, rather than vague promises followed by guilt.

replies.title: A parent makes you feel small in front of other people
replies.short: Made to feel small in public

options.label: Warm (later, in private)
options.text: At dinner, the comment about my weight embarrassed me. Please don't do that in front of people.

options.label: Direct (in the moment)
options.text: Please don't talk about me like that.

options.label: Final (in the moment)
options.text: I'm not going to stay for this. I'll see everyone later.

replies.whenItFits: Private is easier to hear. Use the in-the-moment lines when it continues after you’ve asked.
replies.whenItFitsText: Private is easier to hear. Use the in-the-moment lines when it continues after you've asked.

replies.title: "After everything I've done for you..."

options.label: Warm
options.text: You've done so much for me, and I'm grateful. I still can't do this.

options.label: Direct
options.text: I know you sacrificed a lot. That doesn't change my answer on this.

options.label: Final
options.text: I love you. My answer is still no.

replies.whenItFits: Gratitude and agreement are separate (Chapter 7, Guilt, Favors, and Hidden Debts).
replies.whenItFitsText: Gratitude and agreement are separate (Chapter 7, Guilt, Favors, and Hidden Debts).

replies.title: A parent asks very personal questions

options.label: Warm
options.text: I know you ask because you care. I'd like to keep that part private.

options.label: Direct
options.text: I'm not going to talk about my finances.

options.label: Final
options.text: That's my business. Let's talk about something else.

replies.whenItFits: Questions about money, relationships, health or plans you haven’t decided yet. You can share later if you choose. Privacy isn’t a rejection.
replies.whenItFitsText: Questions about money, relationships, health or plans you haven't decided yet. You can share later if you choose. Privacy isn't a rejection.

replies.title: A call with a parent turns into criticism, and you want to end it

options.label: Warm
options.text: I need to go now. I love you. Talk Sunday.

options.label: Direct
options.text: I'm going to end the call here. We can try again another day.

options.label: Final (if you warned them before)
options.text: I said I'd hang up if this started again, so I'm going to. Talk soon.

replies.whenItFits: Use the final line only if you warned them before. Say it without anger: you are simply doing what you said you’d do.
replies.whenItFitsText: Use the final line only if you warned them before. Say it without anger: you are simply doing what you said you'd do.

replies.title: A parent drops by without warning

options.label: Warm
options.text: I love seeing you. Could you text before coming over, so I can make sure I'm free?

options.label: Direct
options.text: Please text first. If it's not a good time, I'll tell you and we'll pick another.

options.label: Final (when they're at the door)
options.text: I'm not able to have visitors right now. Let's plan for Saturday.

replies.whenItFits: Ask before you’re angry, so it doesn’t sound like an accusation. If they have a key and you’d like it back, that’s a separate conversation; take it gently.
replies.whenItFitsText: Ask before you're angry, so it doesn't sound like an accusation. If they have a key and you'd like it back, that's a separate conversation; take it gently.

replies.title: A relative offers help, but you aren't sure what comes with it

options.label: Warm
options.text: That's generous. Before I accept, is there anything you'd want from me in return?

options.label: Direct
options.text: Are you offering this as a gift, a loan, or an exchange?

options.label: Before accepting
options.text: Let's agree on what each of us is offering first. Then I can give you a clear answer.

replies.whenItFits: Before accepting help with money, housing or a big task. Clear terms protect both of you. For legal or financial questions, get qualified advice before agreeing.
replies.whenItFitsText: Before accepting help with money, housing or a big task. Clear terms protect both of you. For legal or financial questions, get qualified advice before agreeing.

replies.title: Money you thought was a gift is now being called a loan
replies.short: A gift now called a loan

options.label: Warm
options.text: I thought that money was a gift. Can we talk about what each of us understood back then?

options.label: Direct
options.text: I didn't know it was a loan. If you see it that way, let's agree on what's fair and write it down.

options.label: Final
options.text: I'm willing to talk about this once, calmly, with the numbers in front of us. Not at family dinners.

replies.whenItFits: Both of you may honestly remember it differently. Look for any messages from the time, kept somewhere private. For larger sums, talk to a qualified professional before you agree to repay anything.
replies.whenItFitsText: Both of you may honestly remember it differently. Look for any messages from the time, kept somewhere private. For larger sums, talk to a qualified professional before you agree to repay anything.

replies.title: A relative who helped you now expects favors on demand

options.label: Warm
options.text: You helped us so much when we moved. I'm happy to drive you to appointments twice a month.

options.label: Direct
options.text: I can do two Tuesdays a month. I can't be on call every day.

options.label: Final
options.text: Twice a month is what I can give. Let's put the dates in the calendar now.

replies.whenItFits: When you want to give back, but on a scale you can keep up. A limit you hold is kinder than a yes that turns into resentment.
replies.whenItFitsText: When you want to give back, but on a scale you can keep up. A limit you hold is kinder than a yes that turns into resentment.

replies.title: A relative wants you to sign something you haven't read

options.label: Warm
options.text: I want to understand it before I sign. Could you give me a copy to read?

options.label: Direct
options.text: I'm not signing today. I need time to read it and get independent advice.

options.label: Final
options.text: If there's no time for me to understand it, I won't sign.

replies.whenItFits: A family request involving a document you don’t understand. For legal or financial documents, talk to a lawyer or financial adviser who works for you, not for the other person.
replies.whenItFitsText: A family request involving a document you don't understand. For legal or financial documents, talk to a lawyer or financial adviser who works for you, not for the other person.

replies.title: You are expected to care for an aging parent alone

options.label: Warm
options.text: I'm glad to keep doing Dad's appointments. Could you take over the bills and pharmacy runs?

options.label: Direct
options.text: I can't keep doing all of it. Let's list every task this weekend and split them.

options.label: Confirming
options.text: Confirming: I'll keep the appointments, and you'll handle the pharmacy and bills starting on the 1st.

replies.whenItFits: Split the care tasks (driving, bills, groceries, calls). Medical decisions are a separate conversation, with your parent and their doctors. Chapter 26 covers sharing care with siblings.
replies.whenItFitsText: Split the care tasks (driving, bills, groceries, calls). Medical decisions are a separate conversation, with your parent and their doctors. Chapter 26 covers sharing care with siblings.

replies.title: A sibling agreed to help with a parent's care and hasn't

options.label: Warm
options.text: I know it's been a busy month. Are you still able to do the pharmacy runs? If not, let's talk about what you can do.

options.label: Direct
options.text: The pharmacy runs haven't happened for three weeks. Can you do them starting this Friday?

options.label: Final
options.text: If you can't do them, tell me by Friday and I'll set up pharmacy delivery. Then I'd like us to talk about sharing the cost.

replies.whenItFits: Ask before you assume they don’t care. If medication or another essential need is affected, arrange safe cover now with your parent and the relevant service. Discuss costs separately; your sibling has not agreed to pay merely because you asked.
replies.whenItFitsText: Ask before you assume they don't care. If medication or another essential need is affected, arrange safe cover now with your parent and the relevant service. Discuss costs separately; your sibling has not agreed to pay merely because you asked.

replies.title: Pressure about where you spend the holidays

options.label: Warm
options.text: We're spending Thanksgiving with my partner's family this year. We'd love to see you the weekend after.

options.label: Direct
options.text: We've decided to alternate years. This year is the other side.

options.label: Final
options.text: Our plans are set. We'll see you on the 30th.

replies.whenItFits: Decide with your partner first, then tell family together. Offer a real alternative, not a vague “sometime”.
replies.whenItFitsText: Decide with your partner first, then tell family together. Offer a real alternative, not a vague "sometime".

replies.title: A private topic comes up at a family gathering

options.label: Warm
options.text: I'd rather not get into that here. Ask me another time.

options.label: Direct
options.text: I'm not going to discuss that at the table.

options.label: Final
options.text: Not today." (Then change the subject, or leave the room for a minute.)

replies.whenItFits: Your divorce, your weight, your job search, your fertility. You don’t owe the table an update.
replies.whenItFitsText: Your divorce, your weight, your job search, your fertility. You don't owe the table an update.

replies.title: Unasked-for parenting advice from a parent or in-law

options.label: Warm
options.text: Thanks. We've thought about it and decided to do it differently.

options.label: Direct
options.text: We've got this one covered.

options.label: Final
options.text: We've made our decision. I'm not going to go back over it.

replies.whenItFits: Advice given once. Safety issues are different, and worth hearing out. If it’s about your parenting decisions, you and your co-parent decide.
replies.whenItFitsText: Advice given once. Safety issues are different, and worth hearing out. If it's about your parenting decisions, you and your co-parent decide.

replies.title: You're pulled into someone else's family fight

options.label: Warm
options.text: I love you both. I'm not going to get in the middle of this.

options.label: Direct
options.text: That's between the two of you. I'd suggest talking to her directly.

options.label: Final
options.text: I'm not passing messages. Please don't ask me to.

replies.whenItFits: When you’re being asked to carry messages or take sides. Staying out isn’t disloyal. It keeps you from becoming the go-between.
replies.whenItFitsText: When you're being asked to carry messages or take sides. Staying out isn't disloyal. It keeps you from becoming the go-between.

replies.title: An in-law oversteps in your home

options.label: Warm
options.text: I know you're trying to help. Please check with me before moving things in the kitchen.

options.label: Direct
options.text: Please leave the kitchen the way I've set it up. Thanks for understanding.

options.label: Final (to your partner first)
options.text: I need us to agree on this together, and for you to raise it with your mom.

replies.whenItFits: Often the best route goes through your partner, who can talk to their own parent more easily. Agree on a shared position first.
replies.whenItFitsText: Often the best route goes through your partner, who can talk to their own parent more easily. Agree on a shared position first.

replies.title: Repairing after you lost your temper with a parent

options.label: Warm
options.text: I'm sorry I yelled on Sunday. I was frustrated, and I didn't handle it well.

options.label: Direct
options.text: I'm sorry for how I spoke. I still need the comments about my job to stop, and I'd like to talk about that calmly.

options.label: Short message
options.text: I was out of line on the phone. I'm sorry. Can I call you tomorrow?

replies.whenItFits: You can apologize for the yelling and keep the limit. A repair doesn’t mean taking back what you needed.
replies.whenItFitsText: You can apologize for the yelling and keep the limit. A repair doesn't mean taking back what you needed.

replies.title: A friend asks for a favor you don't want to do
replies.short: A favor you don't want to do

options.label: Warm
options.text: Thanks for thinking of me. I can't do that one, but I hope it goes well.

options.label: Direct
options.text: I'm not able to help with that.

options.label: Text
options.text: Can't this time. Hope it works out.

replies.whenItFits: Most ordinary favors. You don’t need a reason. If you’d like to help in a smaller way, see Reply 73.
replies.whenItFitsText: Most ordinary favors. You don't need a reason. If you'd like to help in a smaller way, see Reply 73.

replies.title: An invitation you don't want to accept

options.label: Warm
options.text: I'm going to pass this time. I hope it's a great night.

options.label: Direct
options.text: I won't make it, but thanks for asking.

options.label: Text
options.text: Not this time, but have fun. Send pictures.

replies.whenItFits: Parties, trips, group dinners, weddings that are a stretch. If you’d like to stay close, suggest something you would do: “Coffee next week instead?”
replies.whenItFitsText: Parties, trips, group dinners, weddings that are a stretch. If you'd like to stay close, suggest something you would do: "Coffee next week instead?"

replies.title: A friend keeps asking why you said no

options.label: Warm
options.text: It just doesn't work for me right now. That's really all it is.

options.label: Direct
options.text: I don't have a better reason than that. It doesn't work for me.

options.label: Final
options.text: My answer is the same. Let's talk about something else.

replies.whenItFits: When reasons would only invite “But what if…”. Repeating yourself calmly often settles it. If it doesn’t, ending the topic is your next step.
replies.whenItFitsText: When reasons would only invite "But what if...". Repeating yourself calmly often settles it. If it doesn't, ending the topic is your next step.

replies.title: "A real friend would help"

options.label: Warm
options.text: I care about you a lot. I still can't help with this one.

options.label: Direct
options.text: Being a good friend doesn't mean saying yes to everything.

options.label: Final
options.text: I'm sorry you're disappointed. My answer hasn't changed.

replies.whenItFits: When friendship is used as a test you can only pass by agreeing. Stay warm, and don’t take the bait to prove your loyalty.
replies.whenItFitsText: When friendship is used as a test you can only pass by agreeing. Stay warm, and don't take the bait to prove your loyalty.

replies.title: A friend stops replying after you said no

options.label: Warm
options.text: I've missed hearing from you. If something's bothering you, I'm open to talking.

options.label: Direct
options.text: It feels like things changed after I said no to the trip. I'd like to clear the air.

options.label: Final (if they don't reply)
options.text: I'll leave it with you. I'm here when you want to get in touch.

replies.whenItFits: One honest reach-out, then let them come back in their own time. Chasing over and over usually makes the silence louder.
replies.whenItFitsText: One honest reach-out, then let them come back in their own time. Chasing over and over usually makes the silence louder.

replies.title: A friend keeps canceling at the last minute

options.label: Warm
options.text: I miss you, and the last few plans fell through. Is now a hard time? We can pick something easier.

options.label: Direct
options.text: When plans get canceled on the day, I lose the evening. Can we only book things you're sure about?

options.label: Final (if it keeps happening)
options.text: I'm going to stop setting up plans for a while. Reach out when things settle, and I'll be glad to hear from you.

replies.whenItFits: Ask before you decide they don’t care. Some people are struggling with things they haven’t mentioned.
replies.whenItFitsText: Ask before you decide they don't care. Some people are struggling with things they haven't mentioned.

replies.title: A friend vents to you constantly, and you're worn out

options.label: Warm
options.text: I want to be there for you. I'm wiped tonight. Can we talk Saturday when I can really listen?

options.label: Direct
options.text: Lately most of our calls are about the same problem. I'd love some that are just fun too.

options.label: Final (if it keeps going)
options.text: I care about you, and I can't be your main support for this. Would you think about talking to a counselor?

replies.whenItFits: Ordinary venting. If a friend talks about ending their life or hurting themselves, skip these lines. Call or text the 988 Suicide and Crisis Lifeline for help supporting them, and call 911 in immediate danger.
replies.whenItFitsText: Ordinary venting. If a friend talks about ending their life or hurting themselves, skip these lines. Call or text the 988 Suicide and Crisis Lifeline for help supporting them, and call 911 in immediate danger.

replies.title: Asking a friend for help when you're the one who never asks

options.label: Warm
options.text: I'm not great at asking, but I could really use a ride to the airport early on the 14th. Any chance you're free?

options.label: Direct
options.text: I need a ride to the airport at 6 a.m. on the 14th. Could you do it? Totally fine if not.

options.label: Text
options.text: Big favor to ask, and no is a fine answer: could you drive me to the airport early on the 14th?

replies.whenItFits: Asking balances friendships that run one way. Leave “no” open.
replies.whenItFitsText: Asking balances friendships that run one way. Leave "no" open.

replies.title: A small favor keeps growing

options.label: Warm
options.text: I said I'd help you pack the kitchen. I can't do the whole move, but I'll stay till noon.

options.label: Direct
options.text: I agreed to help pack the kitchen, not to do the whole move. I'm there until noon.

options.label: Final
options.text: Noon is as far as I can go. Good luck with the rest.

replies.whenItFits: Restate what you agreed to, and offer that part fully. The original yes was real. The extra wasn’t part of it.
replies.whenItFitsText: Restate what you agreed to, and offer that part fully. The original yes was real. The extra wasn't part of it.

replies.title: A friend puts you down in front of others
replies.short: Put down in front of others

options.label: Warm (later, in private)
options.text: The crack about my job at the party stung. I don't think you meant it to, but please drop it.

options.label: Direct (in the moment)
options.text: That wasn't funny to me." (Calm, then move on.)

options.label: Final (if it happens again)
options.text: That's the second time I've asked. Please don't do it again.

replies.whenItFits: A short line in the moment beats a long talk in front of everyone.
replies.whenItFitsText: A short line in the moment beats a long talk in front of everyone.

replies.title: Repairing after you let a friend down
replies.short: After you let a friend down

options.label: Warm
options.text: I completely forgot your birthday dinner. I'm really sorry. Can I take you out this week?

options.label: Direct
options.text: I let you down on Saturday, and there's no good excuse. I'm sorry.

options.label: Short message
options.text: I messed up on Saturday. I'm sorry. I'd like to make it up to you.

replies.whenItFits: Own it, offer something concrete, and don’t ask them to make you feel better.
replies.whenItFitsText: Own it, offer something concrete, and don't ask them to make you feel better.

replies.title: Scaling back a yes you gave a friend too fast
replies.short: Scaling back a rushed yes to a friend

options.label: Warm
options.text: I said yes to looking after Pepper for two weeks before I checked my calendar. I'm sorry. I can do the first week, through Sunday the 8th.

options.label: Direct
options.text: I can only take Pepper for the first week. I'm telling you now so you have time to find someone for the second.

options.label: Final (if they push for both weeks)
options.text: One week is what I can do. I'm sorry for the trouble this causes.

replies.whenItFits: When you can still keep part of the promise. Tell them early, and make the part you offer firm, with a date. To withdraw a yes completely, see Reply 16 (Chapter 22, Turn Agreement Into Action).
replies.whenItFitsText: When you can still keep part of the promise. Tell them early, and make the part you offer firm, with a date. To withdraw a yes completely, see Reply 16 (Chapter 22, Turn Agreement Into Action).

replies.title: Someone asks to borrow money

options.label: Warm
options.text: I'm sorry things are tight. I'm not able to lend money right now.

options.label: Direct
options.text: I don't lend money to friends or family. It's a rule that protects the relationship.

options.label: Final
options.text: My answer is no. I hope you find a way through it.

replies.whenItFits: Only use the direct line if it’s true. Offer other help if you like (Chapter 24, Clients, Customers, and Money Decisions).
replies.whenItFitsText: Only use the direct line if it's true. Offer other help if you like (Chapter 24, Clients, Customers, and Money Decisions).

replies.title: Following up on money someone owes you

options.label: Warm
options.text: Hi, I wanted to check on the $300 from January. When do you think you can pay it back?

options.label: Direct
options.text: I need the $300 back by the end of the month. Can you send it by then?

options.label: Text
options.text: Checking in on the $300. Could you send it by the 30th?

replies.whenItFits: Name the amount and a date. Save messages somewhere private. For larger sums, talk to a qualified professional.
replies.whenItFitsText: Name the amount and a date. Save messages somewhere private. For larger sums, talk to a qualified professional.

replies.title: More requests while an old loan is still unpaid

options.label: Warm
options.text: I'd like to help, but I'm not able to lend more until the first loan is sorted out.

options.label: Direct
options.text: The $500 from spring hasn't come back yet, so I can't lend more.

options.label: Final
options.text: No more loans. Once the first one is paid back, we can talk.

replies.whenItFits: Linking the two is fair and easy to explain. You aren’t punishing anyone; you’re declining to add to a debt that hasn’t moved.
replies.whenItFitsText: Linking the two is fair and easy to explain. You aren't punishing anyone; you're declining to add to a debt that hasn't moved.

replies.title: Setting clear terms if you do decide to lend

options.label: Warm
options.text: I'm happy to help. Can we agree on when you'll pay it back, so neither of us has to feel awkward?

options.label: Direct
options.text: I can lend $400. Could you repay $100 a month, starting in March?

options.label: Confirming
options.text: Just confirming: $400 now, $100 a month from March 1st. Thanks for agreeing to that.

replies.whenItFits: After you’ve decided to lend. Keep the written terms private. For financial or legal questions, get qualified advice before agreeing.
replies.whenItFitsText: After you've decided to lend. Keep the written terms private. For financial or legal questions, get qualified advice before agreeing.

replies.title: A borrowed item is never returned

options.label: Warm
options.text: Could you bring the drill back by Friday? I need it for a shelf this weekend.

options.label: Direct
options.text: I need the drill back by Friday. Can you drop it off, or should I swing by?

options.label: Text
options.text: Hey, can I pick up my drill this week? Thursday or Friday?

replies.whenItFits: Make returning it easy: offer a time or to collect it yourself. Most people simply forgot.
replies.whenItFitsText: Make returning it easy: offer a time or to collect it yourself. Most people simply forgot.

replies.title: A "temporary" stay that never ended

options.label: Warm
options.text: When you moved in, we said a few weeks. It's been five months. I'd like us to plan for you to move out by the first of next month.

options.label: Direct
options.text: I need my space back. Let's agree on a move-out date this week.

options.label: Confirming
options.text: Confirming what we agreed: you'll be moved out by March 1st, and I'll help with boxes the weekend before.

replies.whenItFits: Ask to agree a date. Before setting a deadline or taking steps to make someone leave, talk to a housing lawyer or legal aid service. If you feel afraid, skip the script and read Chapter 11; for abuse, the National Domestic Violence Hotline is 1-800-799-7233 (text START to 88788). In immediate danger, call 911.

replies.title: A client is late paying an invoice

options.label: Warm
options.text: Just a reminder that invoice 104 was due two weeks ago. Could you let me know when it's scheduled to be paid?

options.label: Direct
options.text: Invoice 104 is now two weeks overdue. Please pay by the 15th, or let me know if there's a problem with it.

options.label: Final (if it's still unpaid)
options.text: I'll pause new work on the project until the overdue invoice is paid.

replies.whenItFits: Start friendly. Make sure the final line matches your written terms. For large amounts, talk to a qualified professional.
replies.whenItFitsText: Start friendly. Make sure the final line matches your written terms. For large amounts, talk to a qualified professional.

replies.title: An adult son or daughter asks for money again

options.label: Warm
options.text: I love you, and I want you on your feet. I'm not going to send more money.

options.label: Direct
options.text: I can't keep covering rent. I can pay for one session with a budget advisor, if you'd like that.

options.label: Final
options.text: My answer is no on money. I'm glad to help in other ways.

replies.whenItFits: When help has become a pattern that keeps you both stuck. Offering a different kind of help shows you’re still on their side.
replies.whenItFitsText: When help has become a pattern that keeps you both stuck. Offering a different kind of help shows you're still on their side.

replies.title: A salesperson won't let you leave

options.label: Warm
options.text: I appreciate your time. I'm not buying today.

options.label: Direct
options.text: I've heard the offer. My answer is no.

options.label: Final
options.text: I'm going to go now. Thanks." (Then leave.)

replies.whenItFits: A hard sell where you’re free to leave or end contact. You don’t owe a reason or a second listen. If someone blocks your way or threatens you, skip the script, see Chapter 11, and call 911 in immediate danger.
replies.whenItFitsText: A hard sell where you're free to leave or end contact. You don't owe a reason or a second listen. If someone blocks your way or threatens you, skip the script, see Chapter 11, and call 911 in immediate danger.

replies.title: "You have to decide today"

options.label: Warm
options.text: Thanks. I don't make decisions like this on the same day, so I'll pass for now.

options.label: Direct
options.text: If it has to be decided right now, my answer is no.

options.label: Final
options.text: If the offer is still there next week, I'll take a look then.

replies.whenItFits: You need more time to understand the offer. A deadline can be real, and you can still decline rather than decide without enough information (Chapter 10, Charm, Urgency, and the Slow Squeeze).
replies.whenItFitsText: You need more time to understand the offer. A deadline can be real, and you can still decline rather than decide without enough information (Chapter 10, Charm, Urgency, and the Slow Squeeze).

replies.title: A contractor left the job unfinished or poorly done

options.label: Warm
options.text: The fence still isn't finished: the gate and the back section are open. When can you come back to complete it?

options.label: Direct
options.text: The gate and the back section are still open. I'd like the fence completed by the 20th, as agreed.

options.label: In writing (after a call)
options.text: Following up on our call: you agreed to return Tuesday to finish the gate and the back section. Please confirm.

replies.whenItFits: Be specific, with a date. Keep photos and messages somewhere safe. For serious disputes, contact consumer protection or a qualified professional.
replies.whenItFitsText: Be specific, with a date. Keep photos and messages somewhere safe. For serious disputes, contact consumer protection or a qualified professional.

replies.title: A wrong charge or a faulty product

options.label: Warm
options.text: I was charged twice for this order. Could you refund the second charge, please?

options.label: Direct
options.text: I was charged $89 twice for this order. I'd like the second charge refunded today. Can you do that?

options.label: By email
options.text: On the 3rd I was charged $89 twice for order 5521. Please refund the duplicate and confirm by email.

replies.whenItFits: Say what happened and the outcome you want, in one breath. For a faulty product, offering two outcomes you would accept (“a full refund or a replacement”) gives the other person an easy yes.
replies.whenItFitsText: Say what happened and the outcome you want, in one breath. For a faulty product, offering two outcomes you would accept ("a full refund or a replacement") gives the other person an easy yes.

replies.title: Customer service says "There's nothing I can do"

options.label: Warm
options.text: I understand it's not your call. Who can make that decision?

options.label: Direct
options.text: What options do you have? If there are none, please note my request and give me a reference number.

options.label: Final
options.text: Thanks. I'll put this in writing to your complaints team today.

replies.whenItFits: The person on the phone often can’t say yes but can pass you to someone who can. Being calm and specific helps them help you.
replies.whenItFitsText: The person on the phone often can't say yes but can pass you to someone who can. Being calm and specific helps them help you.

replies.title: A client asks for a discount

options.label: Warm
options.text: I want to make this work. At that budget, I can do the first two phases.

options.label: Direct
options.text: My rate stays the same. I can reduce the scope, or we can spread the work over two months.

options.label: Final (if neither option works)
options.text: That price won't work for me. If anything changes, I'd be glad to hear from you.

replies.whenItFits: Trade scope for price. Never bluff about other offers (Chapter 17, Ask for More and Negotiate Well).
replies.whenItFitsText: Trade scope for price. Never bluff about other offers (Chapter 17, Ask for More and Negotiate Well).

replies.title: You're put on the spot to volunteer in front of a group
replies.short: Put on the spot to volunteer

options.label: Warm
options.text: Thanks for thinking of me. I can't take that on this time.

options.label: Direct
options.text: I'm not able to do it. Please count me out.

options.label: Final
options.text: I'm going to pass. I hope someone's able to step in.

replies.whenItFits: If you need to check first, “Let me check my calendar, and I’ll let you know tomorrow” buys a day. Use it only if you really answer tomorrow (Chapter 27, Groups, Media, and Manufactured Pressure).
replies.whenItFitsText: If you need to check first, "Let me check my calendar, and I'll let you know tomorrow" buys a day. Use it only if you really answer tomorrow (Chapter 27, Groups, Media, and Manufactured Pressure).

replies.title: A group chat piles on to get you to agree

options.label: Warm
options.text: I see everyone's keen. It's still a no from me, but have a great time.

options.label: Direct
options.text: I've given my answer. I'm going to step out of this thread until the weekend.

options.label: Final
options.text: My answer is no. I'll mute the chat until the weekend.

replies.whenItFits: Lots of messages can feel like a vote. They aren’t. One clear message, then stepping away from the phone, is usually enough.
replies.whenItFitsText: Lots of messages can feel like a vote. They aren't. One clear message, then stepping away from the phone, is usually enough.

replies.title: A volunteer group keeps asking you to do more

options.label: Warm
options.text: I love being part of this. I can keep doing the newsletter, but not the fundraiser as well.

options.label: Direct
options.text: I'll do one role, not three, and that's the newsletter.

options.label: Final
options.text: I'm only taking on the newsletter this year.

replies.whenItFits: Unpaid roles grow quietly, because the reliable person keeps saying yes. Pick the part you enjoy and hand back the rest.
replies.whenItFitsText: Unpaid roles grow quietly, because the reliable person keeps saying yes. Pick the part you enjoy and hand back the rest.

replies.title: Stepping back from a role you've outgrown

options.label: Warm
options.text: I've loved chairing the committee. At the end of June, I'd like to step back and let someone new take over.

options.label: Direct
options.text: I'm stepping down as chair at the end of June. I'll help train whoever comes next.

options.label: Confirming
options.text: Confirming: my last meeting as chair is June 12th. I'll have the handover notes ready by then.

replies.whenItFits: Give a date and a handover. Leaving well protects the group and your reputation.
replies.whenItFitsText: Give a date and a handover. Leaving well protects the group and your reputation.

replies.title: The bill is split unfairly at a group dinner

options.label: Warm
options.text: I just had the salad and a soda. Is it okay if I pay for mine separately?

options.label: Direct
options.text: I'd rather pay for what I ordered, if that's alright with everyone.

options.label: Before next time
options.text: For the next dinner, could we each pay for our own? It's easier for me.

replies.whenItFits: Say it early, before the card comes out. Most people don’t mind; it just doesn’t occur to them.
replies.whenItFitsText: Say it early, before the card comes out. Most people don't mind; it just doesn't occur to them.

replies.title: A meeting is going in circles and nobody decides

options.label: Warm
options.text: We've covered a lot. What would it take to decide today?

options.label: Direct
options.text: We seem stuck between two options. Can we vote, or agree who makes the call?

options.label: Final (if it's still stuck)
options.text: Could we stop here, send the two options by email, and agree who will decide by Friday?

replies.whenItFits: “Who decides?” is The Power Map (who decides, what each person needs, and where authority, resources and alternatives sit) in one question (Chapter 2, Read the Power Map).
replies.whenItFitsText: "Who decides?" is The Power Map (who decides, what each person needs, and where authority, resources and alternatives sit) in one question (Chapter 2, Read the Power Map).

replies.title: Someone keeps interrupting you in a group

options.label: Warm
options.text: I'd like to finish my point, and then I want to hear yours.

options.label: Direct
options.text: Hang on, I'm not done.

options.label: Final (if it keeps happening)
options.text: I've been interrupted a few times. I'd like two minutes to finish.

replies.whenItFits: Say it calmly and keep going. If it’s a pattern in meetings, ask the person running the meeting to help, before the next one.
replies.whenItFitsText: Say it calmly and keep going. If it's a pattern in meetings, ask the person running the meeting to help, before the next one.

replies.title: "Everyone thinks you're being unreasonable"

options.label: Warm
options.text: I'd be glad to hear from anyone who disagrees. Right now I'm talking with you.

options.label: Direct
options.text: Who specifically? I'd rather hear it from them directly.

options.label: Final
options.text: I'm not going to respond to what unnamed people think.

replies.whenItFits: “Everyone” is often one or two people, or none. Ask for specifics, without making it a trap. If someone does disagree, hear them out.
replies.whenItFitsText: "Everyone" is often one or two people, or none. Ask for specifics, without making it a trap. If someone does disagree, hear them out.

replies.title: The group said yes, but nobody has done anything

options.label: Warm
options.text: At the last meeting we agreed to fix the sign-up sheet. Who's taking that on?

options.label: Direct
options.text: Nothing's happened on the sign-up sheet. Can we name one person and a date right now?

options.label: By email
options.text: Following up from Tuesday: we agreed the sign-up sheet would be updated by the 10th. Who has it?

replies.whenItFits: A group yes with no owner usually means nothing happens. Name one person and one date. That’s The Smallest Agreed Step again.
replies.whenItFitsText: A group yes with no owner usually means nothing happens. Name one person and one date. That's The Smallest Agreed Step again.

replies.title: Repairing after you said something harsh in a group chat
replies.short: Harsh words in a group chat

options.label: Warm
options.text: I was harsh in the chat last night. I'm sorry, especially to the coach. You didn't deserve that.

options.label: Direct
options.text: I'm sorry for the tone of my messages yesterday, to everyone here and especially to the coach. I'll take my questions about the schedule to him directly.

options.label: Private message
options.text: I came across badly in the group yesterday. I'm sorry. Can we talk?

replies.whenItFits: Apologize where the harm happened. If it was in front of the group, the apology belongs there too. Add a private word to the person most affected.

outro.heading: Where to go from here
outro.html:
A good reply gets you through one moment. If the same moment keeps coming back, the book goes deeper.

  • If you keep replaying the same guilt line, read Chapter 7, Guilt, Favors, and Hidden Debts, and Chapter 3, The Rules You Never Chose, which explains The Good Person Contract (the unspoken rules that turn kindness and duty into automatic self-sacrifice).
  • If you freeze and say yes before you’ve thought, practice Notice, Pause, Hold (see the pattern, make room to choose, follow through) and The Choice Check (What happened? What am I assuming? What do I actually owe? What options do I have?) from Chapter 5, Stay Steady Without Going Cold.
  • If you want to ask for more, start with Chapter 17, Ask for More and Negotiate Well, and Chapter 23, Work, Pay, and Recognition.
  • If people say yes and then nothing happens, read Chapter 22, Turn Agreement Into Action.
  • If the answer stays no, Chapter 28, When They Still Say No, helps you build your next step.
  • For a parent, a sibling or an aging parent’s care, see Chapter 26, Family, Friends, and the Roles That Stick. For an ex or a partner, see Chapter 25, Dating, Intimacy, and Difficult Relationships.
  • For daily practice, the 21-Day Power Reset in Part VII turns these replies into habits, one small exercise at a time.

And if anything here touches on fear or danger, go straight to Chapter 11, When Pressure Becomes Danger.
